newsitem.title: UK: UK mortgage lending highest since 1990 - Barclays.
newsitem.headline: UK mortgage lending highest since 1990 - Barclays.

text.p: Mortgage lending in Britain has recovered to its highest level since 1990 but a shortage of available property remains a problem for the housing market, the mortgage arm of Barclays Plc said on Friday.
Barclays Mortgages said it expected total gross lending to amount to 71 billion pounds in 1996, the highest since 1990.
The value of gross mortgage advances in December was up 24 percent on December 1995, it said, although it was 10 percent lower than in November, in line with seasonal trends.
The index also showed mortgage advances in the final quarter of last year were 31 percent up on Q4 1995.
But there remains a significant imbalance between supply and demand in the UK housing market.

Barclays Mortgages' consumer confidence survey found only one homeowner in 13 would be prepared to put their property on the market this year, while one-in-six said they would start to look for new homes.
The vast majority of those surveyed, 83 percent, said they would be unlikely to move house in the next 12 months.

The Barclays Mortgage index measures gross new mortgage advances based on the flow of funds through solicitors' accounts. Its consumer confidence research surveys around 1,000 people over the age of 20 each month.
